properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor lot lines (lots 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A010, 8719A003) bounding the lobe the plan's Block K occupies (lot 8719A010 carries a recorded drop date of March 18, 2025 in the Assessor data (DataSF Parcels, read October 12, 2026) while still flagged active; the dataset does not say why), cross-checked against Mission Rock Design Controls Figure 6.2 (p.151) and the Block K standards sheet (Appendix p.198).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Mission Rock Design Controls' own Figure 6.2 (Maximum Height Plan, p.151) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar and street grid, not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 5 real street-intersection control points (3rd St x Channel St, 3rd St x Long Bridge St, 3rd St x Mission Rock St, Bridgeview Way x Mission Rock St, Terry A. Francois Blvd x Mission Rock St), fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py and matched to their pixel positions in the diagram, then fit as a least-squares affine transform (never fewer than 5 points spanning the whole site, not just 1-2 nearby anchors). Cross-validated against the diagram's own printed scale bar and against the real, independently-confirmed positions of Verde, The Canyon, Building B, and Visa HQ (Building G) -- all four fell inside their correct named blocks under this transform, which is what caught and fixed an earlier, much worse-fitting 4-point version of this same transform (a block letter read one row off, producing 75m of error) before it was used for anything. Residual error against the 5 control points is roughly 3-13m. RETRACED 2026-09-17 (brief docs/briefs/mission-rock-geometry.md; definition of done in docs/site-definition-of-done.md). (1) SOURCE. This file's source_doc_urls pointed at the March 2012 'Design + Development Revised Proposal' (90 pages, no Figure 6.2) while the text cited the Design Controls, so the original pixel measurements could not be reproduced. Redone from the adopted Mission Rock Design Controls (April 24, 2018, sfport.com), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151), rendered ONCE at 300 dpi to data/manual/_reference/mission_rock_dc_p151.png (3300x2550 px, full page). Every pixel measurement below is from that one render. (2) TRANSFORM (one for the whole figure). Since this file was first traced, the Assessor subdivided Seawall Lot 337 (recorded 2020-06-12, mapped 2021-04-13): the four Phase 1 blocks are real lots -- A/The Canyon 8719B002, G/Visa 8719A008, B 8719C003, F/Verde 8719C001 -- whose recorded areas match the plan's block areas within 3%. The figure's drawn corners of A, B, F and G (colour contours, OpenCV) were matched to those 16 real lot corners and a least-squares affine transform fitted: RMS residual 0.67 m, worst corner 1.39 m (n=16); scale 0.2570 m/px (x) and 0.2598 m/px (y), ratio 0.989; axis angle 89.88 deg, i.e. no shear. The figure's own printed 200 ft scale bar measures 239 px on the same render = 0.255 m/px, agreeing within 2%. lon = 2.9127666757282e-06*px + 2.2156884853242e-07*py + (-122.39479060102); lat = 1.6823215817497e-07*px + -2.3273617315092e-06*py + 37.77752553008. (3) VALIDATION on real lines NOT used in the fit: traced C and D west corners fall 0.2-2.4 m from the 3rd Street property line (west edge of the undivided remainder lot 8719A006); D and H south corners 0.1-1.5 m from the Mission Rock Street property line (south edge of 8719A006); J, I and H east corners 1.1-2.8 m from the Terry A Francois Boulevard property line (east edge of 8719A006 / west edge of the TAFB lot 8719A003); the traced Block K corners fall 0.7-1.3 m from the corners of the lobe of the park lot 8719A005 that K occupies. Bearing check, the shear test that Pier 70's point check missed: real 3rd St property line 355.6 deg vs figure 355.3; real TAFB property line 355.7 vs figure 356.1; DataSF Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) centerline 85.7 deg vs the figure's Exposition axis 84.9 deg, with 0.2 m offset at mid-block. (4) METHOD. Each block's fill (base colour plus hatched upper-building zone) was isolated by colour saturation inside a pixel window, its outer contour extracted and simplified (approxPolyDP, 1% of perimeter), transformed, and then any vertex within 3 m of a recorded lot line of 8719A006, 8719A003, 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A009, 8719A010, 8719C001, 8719C002, 8719C004 or 8719D001 was snapped onto that line, so street frontages and shared edges are the Assessor's lines rather than the figure's 1-3 m of contour noise. Cross-checked against an independent trace of the same block on Figure 1.1 (p.10) through its own transform fitted the same way (RMS 1.1 m). (5) CHECKER. Registered in src/verify_block_fill.py under site 'mission_rock' (pixel window and colour rule recorded there); CI prints the IoU against the figure's own fill on every run. K SPECIFICS: the traced Figure 6.2 corners of K fall 0.7-1.3 m from the four corners of a lobe of the park lot 8719A005 that lies south of the park's recorded south line, between the Bridgeview paseo lot 8719A007 (west), the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 (south) and the Terry A Francois Boulevard lot 8719A003 (east) -- a lobe measuring 139 ft x 143 ft, exactly Block K's dimensions on Appendix p.198. So Block K is written as that lobe, using the lots' own recorded vertices (17,880 sf vs 17,829 sf in the 2012 parcel table and 17,384 sf for the raw figure trace). China Basin Park (mission_rock_china_basin_park.geojson) is the same lot minus this lobe, so the two touch exactly and the park's fill no longer hides a planned block. Satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery, 2024 or later: Phase 1 towers and the park are present) shows the lobe as paved staging/turnaround space, not lawn. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) the statement above that the four Phase 1 lots' recorded areas match the plan's block areas 'within 3%' is corrected. Computed from the DataSF Parcels shapes (data/raw/parcels.geojson, projected to EPSG:2227) against the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table (p.30), the recorded areas are A/8719B002 41,986 sf vs 43,413 sf (-3.3%), B/8719C003 40,285 sf vs 41,101 sf (-2.0%), F/8719C001 25,113 sf vs 25,110 sf and G/8719A008 33,058 sf vs 33,055 sf, i.e. within 3.3%, with A just outside 3%; the lot-to-building mapping for B, F and G was not checked against a source in this file. (b) 'the March 2012 Revised Proposal' (src-d4d) is the developer's proposal, not an adopted Design for Development; the adopted document used for the trace is the Design Controls dated April 24, 2018. No geometry was changed. (c) K SPECIFICS: the lobe measures 139 x 143 ft in this file's own trace, while the Design Controls' Appendix p.198 (Block K standards) gives 139 ft x 144 ft (with a 113 ft side; dimensions are 'illustrative'), so 'exactly Block K's dimensions' overstates the match (it agrees to within about 1 ft). (d) The statement that satellite imagery shows the lobe as paved staging/turnaround space, not lawn, cites no image source and has not been re-verified here; treat it as unconfirmed (src/satellite_check.py can check it). 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE but high confidence: every edge is a recorded DataSF lot line (the Assessor has not made Block K its own lot; it is still part of the China Basin Park lot 8719A005 as of the parcels fetch), and the Design Controls figure trace agrees with those lines within 1.3 m at every corner. Planned, unbuilt residential block (120 ft maximum height). ANGLE CHECK: check_geometry_quality.py flags a 12.3-12.6 deg corner here (its tolerance is 12 deg). Every vertex of this polygon is a real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corner (see digitization_method) -- the deviation is the real lot's own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted; see docs/site-definition-of-done.md.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Block K's land is still part of lot 8719A005 (China Basin Park), a lot recorded 2020-06-12 in DataSF's Assessor parcels (data/raw/parcels.geojson, fetched from DataSF Parcels acdm-wktn); the lot lines around it exist but the Assessor has not split K off in that data. Joining status.csv to 8719A005 would show the park and the block as one shape.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a block of the Mission Rock Design Controls' Land Use Plan (dated April 24, 2018), unbuilt as of the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update (which describes the site as 'a surface parking lot' and puts Phase 2 construction 'as early as 2027'), with no distinct real parcel yet. See accuracy_caveat.'. 2026-10-12 accuracy audit follow-up: (a) the method text above (point (4)) calls lots 8719A006, A003, A005, A007, A009, A010, C001, C002, C004 and D001 'recorded lot lines'. They are the lot lines in the Assessor data, but DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn, data_as_of 2026-10-01, read 2026-10-12) shows 8719A009, 8719A010, 8719C002 and 8719D001 (and also 8719A004 and 8719B003) with date_rec_drop 2025-03-18 and project_id_drop 2025P8719 while active is still true; no reason is given in the dataset, so those lines may no longer be current legal boundaries. Lots 8719A006, A003, A005, A007, C001 and C004 carry no drop date. No geometry was changed. For this block the lobe is bounded by 8719A005, A007, A010 and A003; only the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 carries a drop date, so 'every edge is a recorded lot line' is read as 'follows a lot line in the Assessor data' (accuracy_caveat and digitized_from now say so). (b) The sentence 'China Basin Park is the same lot minus this lobe, ... exactly Block K's dimensions' is superseded by entry (c) of the 2026-09-29 audit above: the lobe measures 139 x 143 ft in this file's trace against 139 x 144 ft on Design Controls Appendix p.198. (c) The satellite-imagery statement ('paved staging/turnaround space, not lawn') still cites no image source and was not re-verified on 2026-10-12; entry (d) above stands and it should be read as unconfirmed. ((d)) The sentence in point (2) naming the Phase 1 lots (A/The Canyon 8719B002, G/Visa 8719A008, B 8719C003, F/Verde 8719C001) is only partly supported by a source. F = Verde = 8719C001: SF YIMBY (2024-04-26) files the Verde article under '1070 Bridgeview Way' and DataSF lists 8719C001 at 1070 Bridgeview Way. G = Visa: SF YIMBY (2022-06-03) captions a photo 'Mission Rock Block G northeast view, design by Henning Larsen Architects' and writes 'Visa’s future global headquarters ... showcasing the sharp design by Henning Larsen Architects'; DataSF lists 8719A008 at 300 Toni Stone Crossing, but no source read ties that address to Block G or to Visa (the Henning Larsen project page cited earlier could not be opened on 2026-10-12: HTTP 404), so the lot-to-Visa link is a position match. For A (The Canyon, 8719B002, 1011-1023 3rd St) and B (8719C003, 1089 3rd St) no source read ties the lot to the block letter; those two pairings rest on position and area only. 2026-10-13 (text only; no change to the shape): the sentence that named the public data repository's address was reworded to refer to this shape's mapping log by name, so no raw repository address prints on the page. The tracing history is unchanged.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: every edge follows a DataSF lot line (one of them, the Exposition Street lot 8719A010, carries a recorded drop date of March 18, 2025 in the Assessor data (DataSF Parcels, read October 12, 2026) while still flagged active; the dataset does not say why; the Assessor has not made Block K its own lot; it is still part of the China Basin Park lot 8719A005 in the most recent DataSF Assessor parcel data checked), and the Design Controls figure trace agrees with those lines within 1.3 m at every corner. Planned, unbuilt residential block (120 ft maximum height). ANGLE CHECK: one corner here is 12.3-12.6 degrees off square, beyond the 12-degree tolerance of Pier & Point's automated shape check. Every vertex of this polygon is a real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corner (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log) -- the deviation is the real lot's own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted as a known exception.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Block K's land is still part of lot 8719A005 (China Basin Park), a lot recorded 2020-06-12 in DataSF's Assessor parcels (the DataSF Parcels dataset); the lot lines around it exist but the Assessor has not split K off in that data. Using lot 8719A005 would show the park and the block as one shape.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use, fronting China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry along Terry A. Francois Blvd. Max height 120 ft -- tied for the lowest residential height limit on the site (Flex Blocks H, I and J also allow 120 ft if residential, Figure 6.2 p.151); the March 2012 Revised Proposal's narrative says 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park,' preserving sightlines/stepping the skyline down toward the water. Originally slated for Phase 1 (with A, B, G) before a real, Port-confirmed 2019 swap with Block F -- the sponsors proposed changing Phase 1 from {A, B, G, K} to {A, B, G, F} to accelerate ~100 more units (~40 more affordable) and create a four-corner pedestrian intersection instead of a linear one; an interim-parking-preservation rationale sometimes cited for this swap is not supported by any source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a block of the Mission Rock Design Controls' Land Use Plan (dated April 24, 2018), no source read reports construction on it. The Port's June 5, 2026 Phase 2 update says the work could 'begin construction as early as 2027' (an expected start, not a scheduled one) and does not name this block; its goal of transforming 'a surface parking lot' describes the Mission Rock project site as a whole, not this block's current condition. There is no distinct real parcel yet. See the accuracy note for this shape.
